newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish business urge better ties with EU.
newsitem.headline: Turkish business urge better ties with EU.

text.p: Turkey's Economic Development Foundation (IKV), a leading private sector group, accused the Turkish government on Thursday of being reluctant to improve the relations with the European Union (EU).
"One of the main problem is lack of political dialogue between Turkey and the EU," IKV chairman Meral Gezgin Eris told reporters.
IKV is a leading non-governmental Turkish instutition which lobbies to improve Turkey's ties with the European Union.

Eris said Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamist-led government was more interested in improving relations with the countries outside the EU at a time when Turkey is in an integration period with the Union due to a customs pact.
The customs union took effect in January.
The European parliament said last month it would block multi-million dollars of aid to Turkey from its 1997 budget because of its shaky human rights record.
Eris said uncertainty on the release of the aid would become clear after European Commision report on Turkey was released.
"As the IKV, we represent Turkey's private sector in the best way in the EU. But we are not in a position to fulfill our politicians' gap," she said.
Eris said IKV had also signed an 500,000-ECU financing agreement with the EU to be used for personnel training for an information network. --Istanbul newsroom, +90-212-275 08 75
